data.hypothesis: The baseline and previous lead-directed candidate retain the same general scalar width dispatch, but the latter was slower. This pure-scalar variant tests whether aggregating per-sequence validity predicates with bitwise OR, rather than short-circuit OR, reduces control-flow or dependency overhead on mixed-width input. It keeps the ASCII scan and checks remaining length before every continuation-byte load. The compiler may produce equivalent code or the extra predicate work may outweigh any benefit; performance is unmeasured.

memory_lessons.applicability: Relevant when evaluating branch-reduced scalar UTF-8 validators on this workload.
memory_lessons.claim: The lead-directed scalar candidate was valid but measured slower than baseline: 56.50 µs versus 49.62 µs mean. This does not establish why it regressed.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this isolated predicate-aggregation variant; do not attribute any outcome to branch reduction without controller measurements.

data.notes: Earlier variants to report: the compact-state DFA development attempt was incorrect (cause unspecified); the lead-directed scalar decoder was valid but slower than baseline (56.50 µs versus 49.62 µs mean). This predicate-aggregation candidate is unmeasured; no speedup is claimed. It is a pure-scalar experiment.
transformations: Keep the scalar ASCII-run fast path and existing width-specific decoding structure.
After each width-specific bounds check, load the required continuation bytes and combine all continuation and lead-boundary predicates using non-short-circuit bitwise OR.
Use remaining-length checks before continuation-byte reads to retain safe bounds behavior for all input lengths.
